project: Rudolf Blaschka America 1892 — transport, reference media, split workshop and receiving reconstruction
current_thesis: The 1892 journey intervened in an already distributed Harvard–Hosterwitz reference-supply system whose seeds, roots, gardens, books and detached fresh material still left important American forms inaccessible. Rudolf's travel relocated part of reference selection into the maker's field encounter, where plants were selected or rejected and assigned to drawings, dried specimens, preserved material, seeds, bulbs or living carriage. These reference packets then moved asynchronously through caches and relays while Rudolf continued travelling. Cambridge filtered them against collection needs and translated the returned stock into projected years of future work. Later Hosterwitz production selectively reactivated only some reference lineages as glass. Finished models in turn had to be rebuilt into freight assemblages, customs objects and installed museum objects, and installation could itself generate renewed movement, breakage and repair. Transport therefore redistributed work in space, time, media and authority by repeatedly changing what counted as the movable or usable object.

quantitative_rules: Never use a single 'species collected' total for the expedition.
Attach every number to actor, date, medium/operation and temporal status: observed, selected, drawn, studied, preserved, forecast, reported, dispatched, modelled or converted to years of work.
Preserve ~100/106/116 Jamaica as separate forecast, self-count and institutional drawing ledger until direct reconciliation exists.
Preserve Rudolf ~3-year and Goodale ~4-year work-horizon estimates as actor-specific forecasts.
Treat San Diego 25 -> 36 as closed temporal progression, not contradiction.
Keep packet quantities separate from species-study and model-output counts.
public_map_guard: Do not add more generic geographic lines. New findings should enter through packet cards, media-switch diagrams, object-state timelines and evidence/detail layers. Failed/cancelled access, cache/relay functions and within-building installation states should not be forced into route geometry.
